name: Discovery/Collection — Bulk LDAP Directory Dump (large data, few sessions)
description: A client pulled a large volume of LDAP/LDAPS data (>=40 MB) from directory servers in very few sessions (<=200 flows) — the fingerprint of a directory dump (BloodHound/ldapsearch), as opposed to normal apps that make thousands of small LDAP lookups. Catches the confirmed 251 MB Aug-5 dump AND smaller partial dumps. Native (FortiGate), independent of Defender/MDI.
note:
### Investigation
1. Is source.ip an identity-management/sync server (expected bulk LDAP) or a workstation/Kali/jump host?
2. `ldap_mb` = data exfiltrated from the directory; `flows` low = single bulk operation.
3. Correlate with spray/Kerberoast/lateral from same source (multi-stage rule).
### Tuning
Recurring legitimate bulk-LDAP servers (e.g. an IDM/proxy at 10.11.44.1) should be VALIDATED and suppressed by source.ip. FortiGate double-logs flows across 2 firewalls (~2x byte inflation) — thresholds account for this.
author: raadabujaish
false_positives: Identity-management / directory-sync / LDAP-proxy servers performing legitimate bulk reads (validate and suppress by source.ip).
query:
FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-*
| WHERE destination.port IN (389, 636) AND source.ip IS NOT NULL
| STATS ldap_mb = SUM(destination.bytes)/1000000, sent_mb = SUM(source.bytes)/1000000, flows = COUNT(*), dst_dcs = VALUES(destination.ip), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source.ip
| WHERE ldap_mb >= 40 AND flows <= 200
| SORT ldap_mb DESC
